column4: The crow يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ scratches open the soil to teach how to يُوَارِى the brother's body; it supplies both the section's bull-like earth-scratching verb and the concealment branch of the fire-producing root, while burial reverses the grave-opening scene.
وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ repeats the section's exact grave-overturning verb and scene outside surah 100.

Immediately after the graves are overturned in 82:4, each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind; this makes explicit the same passage from opened graves to disclosed knowledge that 100:9 frames with “does he not know?”
وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا pictures the earth ejecting its burdens, matching the section's treatment of those in graves as contents or a load brought out of soil.
وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ makes the stretched earth cast out “what is in it” and empty itself, an exact parallel to the section's attention to مَا فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ as contained matter.
Allah's raising مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ states as a resurrection promise what the section renders physically as opening soil and extracting its grave contents.
Creation from earth, return into it, and a second خروج from it give the complete three-stage movement behind burial and its reversal in the section.
People come out of the graves كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ; the ayah fuses the section's grave extraction with its named secondary image of locusts springing into motion.
وَأَثَارُوا ٱلْأَرْضَ uses the same root for earlier peoples' plowing and developing the land; their worldly turning of soil is set inside a warning about their eventual destruction.
لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ describes a cow not trained to plow, directly realizing the section's dictionary picture of the ox by which earth is stirred.
Winds تُثِيرُ سَحَابًا, then the cloud revives dead land, and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ; it joins the named root's stirring sense to resurrection from earth.
Winds فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا use the section's ث و ر root for setting a previously still mass in motion, the same core movement behind hooves raising soil.
The earth تَشَقَّقُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا, splitting away from people as they emerge rapidly; this is the grave soil physically opening and surrendering what it held.
At the trumpet blast people rush مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ to their Lord, a direct staging of occupants extracted from their burial places.
They emerge مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا, making the section's overturned grave contents a rapidly moving human multitude.
ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُۥ فَأَقْبَرَهُ makes burial itself an act in the divinely ordered human sequence and supplies the section's ق ب ر root in its literal resting-place sense.
After God causes the person to be buried in 80:21, ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُ reverses that placement by raising him whenever He wills.
Allah returns humans into the earth and then يُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا, stating burial and forceful extraction in the same ayah.
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا presents earth as a containing receptacle, matching the section's focus on graves as lowered, concealed storage.
أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْوَٰتًا identifies the living and the dead as what earth gathers into the receptacle named in 77:25, restoring persons behind the section's content-like مَا.
فِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ ... وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ locates death in earth and later emergence from it, the same closing and reopening of soil developed in the section.

قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ answers the problem of bodies consumed in soil with divine knowledge, directly complementing the question about knowing when grave contents are brought out.
أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى تُورُونَ uses the same و ر ي root in its fire-kindling branch, which the section deliberately sets beside that root's concealment branch.
The devil seeks لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا, bringing into view what had been concealed; the passive وُۥرِىَ realizes the section's named hiding sense and its reveal/conceal reversal.
Flood foam and smelting dross pass away while useful matter remains; this is the Qur'an's clearest assay image for the section's mining soil being worked until valuable metal is separated from waste.

A treasure lies beneath the wall until the orphans can يَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا; a valuable hidden under earth is preserved and later extracted, exactly the buried-treasure model the section gives for grave contents.
Allah يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ, bringing forth what is hidden in the earth; the act condenses the section's movement from concealment below ground to extraction.

After a concealed killing, وَٱللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ promises that God will bring out what was hidden; beside the plowing cow of 2:71, it joins soil-working, homicide, and disclosure as the section does.
The slain person is made alive through the cow and كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَى; it completes 2:71-72 by turning a disputed hidden corpse into evidence of resurrection.

Even a mustard seed hidden in a rock, the heavens, or the earth يَأْتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُ; the minute concealed content is recovered, and the ending ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ echoes the section's final divine awareness.

God separates ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ and piles the bad بَعْضَهُۥ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ; the ayah combines the section's assay-like separation of value with its dictionary picture of mixed goods turned one over another.
يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ makes the resurrection day a testing and exposure of secrets, directly corresponding to the section's ore-like extraction of what chests conceal.

لِيَبْتَلِىَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ joins testing breast contents to purification, closely matching the section's image of processing mixed earth to isolate what is truly there.
Those with diseased hearts suppose that God will not يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَٰنَهُمْ; the verb turns concealed rancor into something extracted from an inner container.
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا تَحْذَرُونَ threatens to bring out what hypocrites fear will be exposed from their hearts, an explicit inner analogue to opening graves and extracting ore.
Whether people hide مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ or show it, Allah knows it; the ayah gives the concealment/disclosure polarity behind the section's chest-as-deposit image.
People fold their breasts and cover themselves to hide, yet God knows what they keep secret and disclose; bodily acts of covering fail to keep chest contents inaccessible.
Concealed or open speech is equally known because إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ, directly pairing secrecy with knowledge of the inner deposit that the section pictures as extracted.

جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا turns the town's upper part into its lower; it is the precise spatial converse of the section's dictionary gloss “made its lower part its upper,” giving physical form to total overturning.
فَجَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا repeats the upper-to-lower inversion, the same complete reversal of levels invoked by the section's explanation of بعثر.
The earth's own violent earthquake initiates the sequence whose next act is ejecting its burdens, so it supplies the ground-upheaval immediately preceding the section's extraction image.
وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ stretches the earth immediately before it casts out its contents, establishing the transformed ground on which the section's “what is in it” scene occurs.

Barren earth اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ after rain and brings forth growth; within the argument that leads to raising those in graves, hidden life stirring through soil becomes evidence for human resurrection.
Rain brings produce out of a dead land and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ, explicitly making emergence from revived soil the model for bringing out the dead.
God brings living from dead and revives earth after its death, then says وَكَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ; biological extraction, revived soil, and human emergence are made one pattern.
The command to look at how God revives earth after its death concludes that He revives the dead, turning the worked soil image into resurrection evidence.
Humbled earth اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ when watered, and its reviver is said to revive the dead; the formerly sunken surface moving and swelling answers the section's hidden-then-rising motion.
Measured water revives a dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ explicitly maps that emergence onto human resurrection.
Rain revives بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ, naming renewed earth as the likeness of the خروج from burial developed in the section.
God revives dead earth and أَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا, bringing grain out of it; the soil releases a useful hidden content just as graves and mineral earth yield what they hold.
After a single blast, فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ places the dead suddenly upon the open surface, the endpoint of the section's movement from concealed depth to exposed ground.
وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ brings a buried girl forward as a questioned moral subject; it restores personhood where burial had reduced a human being to concealed earth-content.
The condemned wish the earth were levelled over them, yet لَا يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثًا; imagined covering by earth cannot prevent disclosure, reversing burial's concealing function.

The earth swallows Qarun and his house, moving a person and his wealth downward into concealment; the section's grave and treasure image runs this motion backward by forcing earth to release its load.
Those فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ cannot presently be made to hear; this closed, silent grave state is the temporal boundary reversed when graves are opened and their occupants emerge.
The question أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ depicts a girl deliberately hidden in soil; its shameful human act of concealment is morally reversed by the later divine exposure of the buried.
The sky splitting begins the sequence that reaches grave overturning in 82:4; one enclosing boundary after another gives way before hidden grave contents do.
Stars scatter immediately before seas burst and graves are overturned; their dispersal parallels the section's dictionary sense of a load broken up and strewn about.
The seas are made to burst forth just before the graves are overturned, extending the scene of breached containers releasing what had been held within.
After earth ejects its burdens, it recounts its news; the opened ground becomes a witness rather than a silent cover, extending the section's move from concealment to knowledge.
People issue forth in separate groups to be shown their deeds after earth has expelled its loads, identifying the ejected contents with accountable persons and their inner record.
The smallest weight of good is made visible after the earth's upheaval, giving a moral assay to the section's image of separating value from worked material.
The smallest weight of evil is likewise made visible, completing the assay-like disclosure rather than allowing any hidden residue to remain mixed in.

Between the revived-earth demonstration and the promise to raise those in graves, this ayah states that God is truth, gives life to the dead, and is capable of all things; it articulates the inference joining the two scenes.

Those emerging in 36:51 ask who raised them from their resting place and are told this is the Merciful's promise, interpreting the opened burial place as promised resurrection rather than mere disturbance.
Allah caused humanity to grow from the earth like vegetation; paired with return and extraction in 71:18, it makes soil both origin and temporary repository.
The objection أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا نَّخِرَةً identifies decayed bones as the material awaiting the sudden return to the surface in 79:14, specifying what the grave contains.
The single زَجْرَةٌ triggers the sudden appearance on the surface in 79:14, supplying the release event for the section's hidden-to-exposed movement.
On the resurrection day people are كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ, a dispersed insect multitude that nonlexically parallels the section's locusts springing up and 54:7's grave-emergence swarm.
Allah splits seed and date-stone and brings the living from the dead; a closed piece of matter opening to release hidden life parallels the section's soil and grave extraction.
ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ شَقًّا pictures earth deliberately split so that what follows can emerge, an agricultural counterpart to broken grave soil.
وَٱلْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ presents earth by its capacity to fissure, the same opening of a formerly continuous surface required by the section's plowing and unburial images.
Mountains are removed, earth is seen exposed, and all people are gathered with none left behind; the stripped surface corresponds to emptied earth revealing every human it had concealed.
إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ رَجًّا makes earth itself violently convulse on the last day, enlarging the hoof-broken surface into an eschatological ground upheaval.
Mountains are pulverized immediately after earth convulses, supplying the solid material that becomes airborne dust in the next ayah.
فَكَانَتْ هَبَآءً مُّنۢبَثًّا turns pulverized ground into scattered dust in the air, a large-scale counterpart to hooves breaking the surface and raising its particles.

حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ calls entry into graves a “visit”; this makes the grave a temporary stopping place, consistent with the section's lexical description of it as a station that will be opened again.
حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ uses the section's named تَوَارَى form for disappearing behind a veil, showing the hiding branch of و ر ي in a setting distinct from covering a corpse with soil.
The brother is killed and the killer becomes a loser; this supplies the corpse whose exposed state creates the first burial problem solved by the crow in 5:31.
بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ gives the buried girl a charge to answer through no fault of her own, completing 81:8's reversal from concealed object to vindicated person.
People تَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً from the sea, a non-mineral parallel in which valuable adornment is extracted from a larger enclosing medium.
From the two seas people تَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً; the repeated extraction of valuable adornment clarifies the section's concrete mining sense of separating treasure from surrounding matter.
A grain in the darknesses of earth is included among what God knows; the tiny hidden terrestrial content joins burial-like concealment to exhaustive divine awareness.
Whether people reveal what is within themselves or hide it, God calls them to account for it; disclosure is tied to judgment as in the section's transition from grave contents to chest contents.
God knows مَا تُخْفِى ٱلصُّدُورُ, naming breasts specifically as containers of concealed material that remains accessible to divine knowledge.
The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose, restating the section's inner hidden-versus-exposed relation in exact bodily terms.
The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose; the repeated formulation supports the section's claim that inner contents cannot remain buried.

People return to God, are told what they did, and He is عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ; return, disclosure of deeds, and knowledge of breasts form the same eschatological sequence as opened graves and processed hearts.
God knows what people conceal and reveal and is عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ, explicitly locating the hidden deposit in breasts.
أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ answers 67:13's concealed-speech scene by grounding knowledge in creation and ending ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ, close to the section's final insistence on the Lord's awareness.
وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ treats what deniers harbor as something stored up in a container, a close conceptual match for inner contents accumulated and then exposed.
God does not leave believers in a mixed state حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ; this moral separation parallels assaying mixed earth until unlike contents are distinguished.
A barzakh stands behind the dead إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ, defining burial as an interim enclosure with a fixed end rather than a permanent hiding place.

Qarun's treasures have keys heavy for a strong company, making wealth a literal burden before person, house, and riches are swallowed by earth in 28:81; together they invert the section's ejected load and buried treasure.

God makes fire for people from a green tree, so an apparently contrary material releases latent flame; this nonlexically develops the section's sense of fire as something struck or brought forth from concealment.
The human supposes that God will not gather his bones; the ayah identifies disassembled bodily remains as recoverable grave content rather than irretrievable debris.
God is able even to proportion the fingertips, completing 75:3's answer by showing that extraction and gathering do not blur the identity of what earth held.
The objector displays a decayed bone and asks who can revive it, turning the physical remainder associated with a grave into the test case for resurrection.
The answer says the One who originated the bones will revive them and knows every creation, joining restoration of buried remains to the knowledge motif of the section.

The ayah names ٱلْجَرَادَ among the signs sent against Pharaoh; it securely supplies the same creature as the section's dictionary example, though unlike 54:7 it does not itself say that the locusts rise or spread from graves.
